rv: Students are murdered at a WASPy east coast college by a clever killer. Accomplishing the second murder stretches credibility. The story progresses well, but like some 1930s mysteries it lacks background music or camera movement or movement by the actors to make the interminable exposition scenes less boring. I downloaded the MPEG4 file. Video is OK; audio is scratchy.

Charles Starrett before he became the renowned coyboy star was really a down-east rich college boy in real life, and he plays the younger lead with a certain relish. It's a neat little mystery with Starrett as "The Son" and wooden Robert Warwick as "The Father" and it plays like an Ellery Queen yarn and it's not bad. Enjoy.

Another short 1930s mystery - they sure churned them out then - with little action outside of the stage, except for a car ride or two focused on the two front seat occupants and a "stage" scene inside another house - low budget for sure. There are no memorable performances and, as a previous reviewer noted, one murder really "stretches credibility." Nevertheless, it is a reasonably engaging murder mystery with enough suspects to keep you guessing - although none of that matters as last minute revelations tie the whole thing up. Strictly for fans of 1930s murder mysteries who want to see them…

rv: According to my research, the director of this was NOT Willing Forst but the actor Franz Fielder (1902-1965), who also directed similar shorts such as "Alt Berlin - Wie es einmal war" (1934), "Berlin bleibt Berlin" (1935), and "Kleiner Bummel durch Berlin" (1938), which can all be purchased together on one DVD as "Berlin - Hauptstatdt des Deutsches Reiches in Farbe." With regards to the dating: Yes, it can not be 1936 because the Victory Column was not moved to the position shown until 1938 (also, a 4th level was added during its relocation, which can be seen in the film).

Large parts of this movie were shot in 1939 as you can easily see from the "Siegessaeule" which was placed on "Grosser Stern" in 1938/39 and the "Neue Reichskanzlei" which was finished in 1939. Even the text is wrong, identifying the "Neue Reichskanzlei" as "Reichsluftfahrtsministerium".

rv: Overall, I thought it was good. Just a little more intelligent than the typical sitcoms of the day. Jane Powell and Russell Johnson played off of each other pretty well considering it was just the pilot and the first time they'd worked together so closely. I think they would have been pretty good together had it went to series. The costars were cast fairly well, too. I guess our loss was The Beverly Hillbillies' gain in that it freed up Harriet MacGibbon.
Is this an inspiration for Gilligan's Island?

At the least it must have gotten this staid math professor portrayer hired as that staid science professor. There is also the beautiful actress character, the older couple, and the rest of the cast who might be likened to someone on Gilligan's Island if you wanted to stretch the comparison some more. Three stars because of Powell's singing.

I think this show could have made a go of it, if it didn't have so many sub plots in the pilot. Too many different things going on at one time.
